params.prompt: A storybook painting. A wide vista of a forest path on a green hill above a tropical port city, warm afternoon. A dirt path winds beside a small turquoise stream with a wooden plank bridge; a huge old tree with red flowers spreads over the path; in a small clearing in the middle distance, a small homemade satellite dish antenna on a tripod and a little solar panel. Far below and behind, the pale hazy city and river. The student and the cat walk along the path toward the bridge. Foreground framed by dark silhouettes of large tropical leaves and ferns. Tiny in the frame, less than one tenth of the image height: the young engineering student from the first reference image (voluminous dark curly hair, warm brown skin, khaki jacket and cargo pants, brown crossbody bag) and her small gray-taupe cat from the second reference image (cream face and paws, blue collar with a small cyan round tag). Use the references only for their design and colors, and paint both with a few gouache brush strokes in the same style as the scene. Painted as a full-bleed plate from a hand-made illustrated storybook: traditional gouache and transparent watercolor on textured cold-press paper, visible brush strokes, soft wet-in-wet washes with the paper grain showing through, simplified flat shapes with loose painterly edges, very few small details, large calm areas. Restrained warm palette of cream, ochre, terracotta, muted tropical green and petrol-blue shadows; shadows are colored, never black; low saturation. Strong atmospheric perspective: the far distance is pale, hazy and bluish with almost no detail, and only the focal area is a little crisper. Composition in three layered planes like a paper theater: a dark, simple silhouette framing the foreground, the lit middle ground, and a pale background. Matte and handmade: no glossy highlights, no bloom, no lens flare, no light rays, no 3D render look, no digital sharpness, no hyper-detail. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no insignia, no emblems, no flags. No text, no logos, no interface.
